To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mutations of the Wiskot-Aldrich syndrome gene result either in Wiskot-Aidrich syndrome or in X-linked thrombopenia and that the clinical course and prognosis of the patients are different between these two diseases.
WASP expression in patients with mutations of the WAS gene was associated with better clinical outcome, especially in the absence of severe infections and malignancies.
WASP gene mutations are associated with the clinical phenotype of patients with WAS/X-linked thrombocytopaenia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical features of patients with WAS/XLTP.
a new method to determine prognosis in patients with WAS/XIT.
the clinical course and prognosis of Japanese patients with Wiskott-Alderich Syndrome and X-linked thrombocytopathia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence or absence and level of WASP expression is a useful indicator for the prognosis of patients with WAS/XLTP.
the presence or absence and the level of WAS protein expression is the most reliable and important factor for the prediction of the prognosis of patients with WAS/X-linked thrombocypenia (XLT).
the presence or absence (or amount) of WASP protein expression is a good predictor for long-term prognosis of patients with WAS/X-LT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WASP gene mutation is associated with a wide variety of disease severity and that the WASP expression level is a useful tool to predict the disease severity and the prognosis of WAS/XLT patients.

the WASP expression is an important factor to predict prognosis of WAS/XLT patients and that the patients with WASP-negative mutations should be treated by hematopoietic cell transplantation as early as possible.
WAS is a disease with high morbidity and mortality and that hematopoietic cell transplantation is the only curative treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with WASP mutations who do not have WAS protein expression are at high risk of severe disease and that these patients may benefit from stem cell transplantation at an early stage.
WASP expression status is a useful tool to predict long-term prognosis for Japanese patients with WAS/X-linked thrombocytopaenia.
WASP expression is a useful predictor for long-term prognosis for WAS and XLT patients.
